# relweights

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/michaelides/relweights/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/michaelides/relweights/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

relweights computes Johnson's (2000) relative weights. They divide the
explained variance ($R^2$) of a regression among correlated predictors. Each
predictor is credited with its unique contribution and with its share of
what it explains together with the other predictors. The weights are
non-negative and sum to $R^2$.

The analysis works directly on fitted models:

* **linear models** fitted with `lm()`, including models with prior weights;
* **structural equation models** fitted with
  [lavaan](https://lavaan.ugent.be). Every structural regression is
  analysed, including regressions among latent variables, using the
  model-implied correlations, separately for each group and level.

Each analysis returns:

* raw weights and rescaled weights (percentages of $R^2$);
* standardized coefficients and zero-order correlations;
* the signs of the standardized coefficients and of the coefficients of the
  orthogonal counterparts;
* optional bootstrap percentile intervals;
* ggplot2 plots.

## Installation

relweights is not yet on CRAN. Install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/michaelides/relweights):

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("michaelides/relweights", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

## Linear models

```{r lm}
library(relweights)

fit <- lm(mpg ~ cyl + disp + hp + wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
set.seed(2024)
rw <- relweights(fit, bootstrap = TRUE, n_boot = 1000)
rw
```

```{r lm-plot}
autoplot(rw, sign = "beta")
```

## Structural equation models

```{r lavaan}
model <- "
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
  speed ~ visual + textual + ageyr + grade
"
sem_fit <- lavaan::sem(model, data = lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939,
                       group = "school")
rw_sem <- relweights(sem_fit)
rw_sem
```

```{r lavaan-plot}
autoplot(rw_sem, type = "groups")
```

Other plots show how $R^2$ divides among the predictors
(`autoplot(rw, type = "r2")`) and set relative weights next to squared
standardized coefficients and squared correlations
(`autoplot(rw, type = "compare")`).

## Learn more

`vignette("relweights")` covers the method, signs, factors, bootstrap
intervals and the analysis of lavaan models in detail. The test suite checks
the results against the [rwa](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=rwa)
package, which implements relative weights for data frames.

## Citation

If you use relweights in published work, please cite the package:

```{r citation-text, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
relweights_citation <- citation("relweights")
cat(format(relweights_citation, style = "text"), sep = "\n")
```

A BibTeX entry for LaTeX users:

```{r citation-bibtex, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat(c("```bibtex", as.character(toBibtex(relweights_citation)), "```"),
    sep = "\n")
```

Please also cite Johnson (2000) for the relative weights method and, when
you analyse lavaan models, Rosseel (2012); see the references below. In R,
`citation("relweights")` shows this information.

## References

Johnson, J. W. (2000). A heuristic method for estimating the relative weight
of predictor variables in multiple regression. *Multivariate Behavioral
Research, 35*(1), 1--19. <https://doi.org/10.1207/S15327906MBR3501_1>

Rosseel, Y. (2012). lavaan: An R package for structural equation modeling.
*Journal of Statistical Software, 48*(2), 1--36.
<https://doi.org/10.18637/jss.v048.i02>

Tonidandel, S., & LeBreton, J. M. (2011). Relative importance analysis: A
useful supplement to regression analysis. *Journal of Business and
Psychology, 26*(1), 1--9. <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10869-010-9204-3>
